_readme: THE SAME ASTEROID, FROM THE BEACH (2026-10-25; docs/WATER_V2.md section 13). The impact of
impact_orbit.json -- 10 km at 20 km/s into 35 N 42 W at 15:00Z -- is 2,625 km from the Merrimack's
mouth; its first wave arrives on the deep-water clock about 3.7 h later (18:41Z). The scene starts
at 18:20Z and runs 30x: the minute of record is 18:20 to 18:50, the sea rising over the dunes
before the front and the front itself (hundreds of metres at the faces: a 10 km impactor drowns
everything here; impact_newburyport_1km.json is the same shore under a 1 km one). The solver's open faces read the wave's level (laws/Impact.hlsli, Green's law to the
face's depth, unbounded: the solver is the nonlinear reader) and carry it up the river and over Plum Island; the bank and the globe
draw the same law where the solver is silent. No display exaggeration here: the hull and the
solver read the wave raw, and so does the eye. The wave solve keeps its first read of the
solver's current (water.swe.currentRefreshS past the run): at 30x a re-key every 90 sim seconds
is a three-minute solve every three seconds, and a headless record waits for each.
